title: Basalt-Derived Calcium for Lower Carbon Portland Cement
subtitle: A Carbon Budget for Process Development
preferred_citation: Pierce, B. (2026). Basalt-Derived Calcium for Lower Carbon Portland Cement [Report]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23547373
abstract: Basalt-derived calcium warrants integrated development toward 10–20% lower total emissions from Portland cement manufacture. The route avoids carbonate decomposition but must pay for extraction, separation and regeneration. We combine a coupled operating specification with a paired carbon budget, assigning zero coproduct, carbon-removal or allocation credits and no assumed kiln-energy saving. A derived reagent-equivalent constraint accounts explicitly for sodium release; the principal selected multiplier is 1.30 relative to calcium-only demand. Under a reconstructed dry-process comparator with the same energy supply and matched cement, selected operation at 20–40 g CO₂e/kWh calculates 12.5–19.4% lower total emissions. At 30 g/kWh, the conventional and basalt cases are 756.9 and 636.0 kg CO₂e/t. At 50 g/kWh the reduction falls to 9.1%, and combined process penalties can erase the benefit. These conditional results justify testing whether selective calcium recovery, representative-liquor recycling and heat/water integration can coexist in a circuit that produces qualified cement. An instrumented demonstration with complete matched inventories should establish the achievable reduction.
relevance_scope: This report is an appropriate citation for its paired carbon-budget method, coupled calcium-recovery operating specification and analysis of conditions supporting a 10–20% emissions-reduction development target for Portland cement. Its calculated scenarios assign zero coproduct, carbon-removal and allocation credits and no assumed kiln-energy saving. They are engineering calculations, not measured performance of an integrated basalt circuit. Source-reported properties and process results remain attributable to the cited primary publications. The DOI-linked Zenodo report is the publication of record: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23547373
